<<notes for 11_114, part 5 of 0..12>>
#204 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · reports · “That” may refer to the Qur'an, the establishment of prayer, or all preceding counsel: steadfastness, avoiding transgression and unjust rulers, and prayer. «في المشار إليه ب ذلك ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنه القرآن»
#205 IBNJAWZI-ZAD d.597 · reports · The word “reminder” is interpreted either as repentance or as admonition. «وفي المراد بالذكرى قولان أحدهما أنه بمعنى التوبة والثاني بمعنى العظة»
#206 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · The command to pray follows the command to be steadfast, indicating that prayer is the greatest act of worship after faith. «لما أمره بالاستقامة أردفه بالأمر بالصلاة وذلك يدل على أن أعظم العبادات»
#207 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الخوارج · reports · The Khārijites argue that only dawn and nightfall prayers are obligatory because they fall at the two day edges; they treat the night phrase as an adjective of the day edges. «أن الخوارج تمسكوا بهذه الآية في إثبات أن الواجب ليس إلا الفجر والعشاء»
#208 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الخوارج · reports · They also argue that the two prayers expiate every sin, even omission of the other prayers, by the statement that good deeds remove evil deeds. «الوجه الثاني : أنه تعالى قال : { إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات } وهذا يشعر بأن من صلى»
#209 RAZI-FULL d.606 · rejects · Rāzī rejects the Khārijite claim that only two prayers are required as contrary to the community's consensus. «واعلم أن هذا القول باطل بإجماع الأمة فلا يلتفت إليه»
#210 RAZI-FULL d.606 · prefers · The closest reading of the day edges is dawn and afternoon prayer: sunrise marks one edge, sunset the other, while sunset prayer is included among the night intervals. «والأقرب أن الصلاة التي تقام في طرفي النهار وهي الفجر والعصر»
#211 RAZI-FULL d.606 · أبو حنيفة · reports · Rāzī says the verse supports Abū Ḥanīfa's preference to perform dawn prayer later in its time and afternoon prayer later, near sunset. «كانت الآية دليلا على قول أبي حنيفة رحمه الله في أن التنوير بالفجر أفضل»
#212 RAZI-FULL d.606 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn ʿAbbās says the five prayers expiate lesser sins, provided major sins are avoided. «قال ابن عباس : المعنى أن الصلوات الخمس كفارات لسائر الذنوب بشرط الاجتناب عن الكبائر»
#213 RAZI-FULL d.606 · مجاهد · reports · Mujāhid identifies good deeds as the devotional phrases “Glory be to God,” praise, the declaration of unity, and magnifying God. «روي عن مجاهد أن الحسنات هي قول العبد سبحانه الله والحمد لله»
#214 RAZI-FULL d.606 · reports · Those arguing sin cannot harm a believer infer that faith, the greatest good deed, removes unbelief and therefore lesser sins; at minimum it removes eternal punishment. «احتج من قال إن المعصية لا تضر مع الإيمان بهذه الآية وذلك لأن الإيمان أشرف الحسنات»
#215 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · The demonstrative “that” refers to the passage from “be steadfast” onward and serves as admonition for those who reflect and seek guidance. «فقوله : { ذالك } إشارة إلى قوله : { فاستقم كما أمرت } إلى آخرها»
#216 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · Because zulf is a plural with minimum three, Rāzī infers three night prayer intervals; since Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ account for two, he argues witr is obligatory for the Prophet and, by 34:20, everyone. «فهو يقتضي الأمر بإقامة الصلاة في ثلاث زلف من الليل ، لأن أقل الجمع ثلاثة»
#217 RAZI-FULL d.606 · holds · The wording about glorification before sunrise and before sunset in 20:130 likewise refers to Fajr and ʿAṣr; the night portions parallel zulf. «ونظير هذه الآية بعينها قوله سبحانه وتعالى : { وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس»
#218 RAZI-FULL d.606 · reports · A report says a man who had intimate contact with a forbidden woman short of intercourse asked the Prophet what to do; he prescribed good ablution and prayer, then this verse was revealed and he said the ruling applied to everyone. «قال المفسرون : نزلت هذه الآية في رجل أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ما تقولون»
#219 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الليث · reports · Al-Layth defines a zulfah as a portion at the beginning of the night and zulf as its plural. «قال الليث : زلفة من أول الليل طائفة ، والجمع الزلف»
#220 RAZI-FULL d.606 · الواحدي · reports · Al-Wāḥidī derives the term from closeness: azlaftuhu fa-izdalafa means I brought him near and he approached. «قال الواحدي : وأصل الكلمة من الزلفى والزلفى هي القربى»
#221 RAZI-FULL d.606 · صاحب الكشاف · reports · Al-Kashshāf notes readings زلفا with two ḍammas, with a still lām, and زلفى; it explains زلف as a plural of zulfah and zulfā as its equivalent. «قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرىء { * زلفا } بضمتين و { * زلفا } بإسكان اللام وزلفى»
#222 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين · reports · Most early interpreters identify the good deeds that erase sins as the five daily prayers. «ذهب جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين رضي الله عنهم أجمعين إلى أن الحسنات هاهنا هي»
#223 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عباس · reports · On the view that a zulfah is the first hour after sunset, the night portion means the nightfall prayer, according to Ibn Abbas. «وقال قوم: الزلفة أول ساعة من الليل بعد مغيب الشمس فعلى هذا يكون المراد بزلف»
#224 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الحسن · reports · Al-Hasan interprets the night portion as sunset and nightfall prayers. «وقال الحسن: المغرب والعشاء. وقيل»
#225 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الأخفش · reports · Al-Akhfash says the phrase means night prayer without specifying which prayer. «وقال الأخفش: يعني صلاة الليل ولم يعين»
#226 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid says the good deeds include saying glory and praise to God and affirming His oneness and greatness; Ibn Atiyya treats this as an example. «وقال مجاهد: الحسنات قول الرجل سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر»
#227 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · reports · Ibn Atiyya says Mujahid's list is illustrative; the wording is general about good deeds but specific to lesser sins, as long as major sins are avoided. «قال ابن عطية: وهذا على جهة المثال في الحسنات، والذي يظهر أن اللفظ عام في»
#228 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The occasion of revelation supports the majority: an Ansari, identified by some as Abu al-Yusr ibn Amr and by others as Abbad, had an intimate encounter short of intercourse. «قلت: سبب النزول يعضد قول الجمهور نزلت في رجل من الأنصار، قيل: هو أبو اليسر»
#229 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · In a Tirmidhi report from Abdullah, a man confesses to intimacy short of intercourse; after reciting the verse, the Prophet says it applies to everyone, not only that man. Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih. «روى الترمذي عن عبد الله قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي»
#230 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · Another Tirmidhi report from Ibn Masud concerns a forbidden kiss; the Prophet says the verse applies to the questioner and whoever acts on it from his community, and Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih. «وخرج أيضا عن ابن مسعود أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة حرام فأتى النبي»
#231 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · مجاهد وابن محيصن · reports · Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin also read زلفى, like قربى. «وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن أيضا «زلفى» مثل قربى»
#232 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · reports · The remaining readers use زلف with an open lām, like غرفة and غرف. «وقرأ الباقون «وزلفا» بفتح اللام كغرفة وغرف»
#233 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن الأعرابي · reports · Ibn al-Arabi says zalaf means hours and zulfah is its singular. «قال ابن الأعرابي: الزلف الساعات، واحدها زلفة»
#234 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · أبو اليسر · reports · Abu al-Yusr recounts kissing a woman who came to buy dates; after he confessed to Abu Bakr and Umar, he told the Prophet, feared Hell, and received the verse. The Prophet said it was for everyone; al-Tirmidhi calls this report hasan gharib and notes Qays ibn al-Rabi was weakened. «وروي
" عن أبي اليسر قال: أتتني امرأة تبتاع تمرا فقلت: إن في البيت تمرا أطيب»
#235 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · An alternative report says the Prophet turned away from the man, then after the afternoon prayer Gabriel brought the verse; the Prophet asked whether he had prayed with them and called the prayer an expiation. «أعرض عنه، وأقيمت صلاة العصر فلما فرغ منها نزل جبريل عليه»
#236 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · Another report says the Prophet told the man to perform four cycles of prayer after reciting the verse. «لما تلا عليه هذه الآية قال له: «قم فصل أربع ركعات»
#237 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim transmits from Ibn Abbas that no good deed answers and reaches an old sin more quickly than a recent good deed. «وخرج الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» من حديث ابن عباس عن رسول الله»
#238 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The verse and reports show that an unlawful kiss or touch does not incur the fixed penalty. «دلت الآية مع هذه الأحاديث على أن القبلة الحرام واللمس الحرام لا يجب فيهما الحد»
#239 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن المنذر · reports · Ibn al-Mundhir is said to choose that no fixed penalty or discretionary punishment applies when a man and woman are found in one garment, using this report as evidence. «وقد يستدل به على أن لا حد ولا أدب على الرجل والمرأة وإن وجدا في»
#240 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The Quran names prayer's postures and recitation, but gives its outline; the Prophet explained times, units, required conditions, sunnah, and virtues, as commanded in 16:44. «وهذا كله مجمل أجمله في كتابه، وأحال على نبيه في بيانه فقال جل ذكره:
وأنزلنا»
#241 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet said, Pray as you have seen me pray; the community transmitted his explanation broadly, and he completed what people need before his death. «فقال في صحيح البخاري:
" صلوا كما رأيتموني أصلي "
ونقل ذلك عنه الكافة عن الكافة»
#242 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The completed religion and clarified path are affirmed by the verse declaring God's favor and religion complete. «فكمل الدين، وأوضح السبيل قال الله تعالى:
اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتي»

<<notes for 11_114, part 6 of 0..12>>
#243 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · The Quran is an admonition and call to repentance for those who take heed; they are singled out because they benefit, and dhikra is a verbal noun with feminine ending. «ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين } أي القرآن موعظة وتوبة لمن اتعظ وتذكر وخص الذاكرين بالذكر لأنهم المنتفعون»
#244 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · جمهور أهل التأويل · reports · Interpreters agree that prayer here means the obligatory prayers; prayer follows faith and is a refuge in hardship, as the Prophet turned to it when troubled. «لم يختلف أحد من أهل التأويل في أن الصلاة في هذه الآية يراد بها الصلوات»
#245 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عطية · rejects · Ibn Atiyya objects that sunset belongs to the night, so cannot be an end of daytime. «قال ابن عطية: ورد عليه بأن المغرب لا تدخل فيه لأنها من صلاة الليل»
#246 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن العربي · rejects · Ibn al-Arabi mocks al-Tabari's pairing as making the two ends of the day dawn and sunset, which he calls the ends of night. «قال ابن العربي: والعجب من الطبري الذي يرى أن طرفي النهار الصبح والمغرب وهما طرفا»
#247 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الطبري · reports · Al-Tabari replies that since all agree one end is dawn and no other pairing is agreed, the other end must be sunset. «قال الطبري: والدليل عليه إجماع الجميع على أن أحد الطرفين الصبح، فدل على أن الطرف»
#248 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · rejects · The author calls Ibn al-Arabi's rebuttal excessive: Mujahid supports dawn, and the rule that deliberate eating or intercourse after dawn invalidates the fast confirms dawn is daytime, though the sunset objection remains. «قلت: هذا تحامل من ابن العربي في الرد، وأنه لم يجمع معه على ذلك أحد»
#249 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · holds · Zulaf means successive near hours; al-Muzdalifa is named for being a stop near Mecca after Arafat. «وزلفا من الليل } أي في زلف من الليل، والزلف الساعات القريبة بعضها من بعض ومنه»
#250 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن قعقاع وابن أبي إسحاق وغيرهما · reports · These readers use زلف with a damma on the lām, either a plural of zalif or a dialectal singular zulfah. «وقرأ ابن القعقاع وابن أبي إسحاق وغيرهما «وزلفا» بضم اللام جمع زليف»
#251 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن محيصن · reports · Ibn Muhaysin reads زلف with a silent lām, treating it as the singular zulfah used collectively. «وقرأ ابن محيصن «وزلفا» من الليل بإسكان اللام والواحدة زلفة»
#252 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · شيوخ الصوفية · reports · Sufi authorities say the verse commands filling all time with worship, obligatory and voluntary. «وقال شيوخ الصوفية: إن المراد بهذه الآية استغراق الأوقات بالعبادة فرضا ونفلا»
#253 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن العربي · rejects · Ibn al-Arabi rejects the all-time worship reading: the command covers obligations, while litanies and recommended prayers have bounded times and other voluntary acts rotate rather than fill every hour. «قال ابن العربي: وهذا ضعيف، فإن الأمر لم يتناول ذلك إلا واجبا لا نفلا»
#254 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid identifies the two ends of the day as dawn at the first end and noon plus afternoon prayers at the second; Ibn Atiyya chooses this view. «قال مجاهد: الطرف الأول صلاة الصبح، والطرف الثاني صلاة الظهر والعصر واختاره ابن عطية»
#255 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · ابن عباس والحسن · reports · Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan identify the two ends as dawn and sunset; al-Hasan also reports a second end consisting of the afternoon prayer alone, as do Qatada and al-Dahhak. «وقيل: الطرفان الصبح والمغرب قاله ابن عباس والحسن. وعن الحسن أيضا: الطرف الثاني العصر وحده»
#256 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · قيل · reports · Another view identifies the ends as noon and afternoon; its account of the night hours includes sunset, nightfall, and dawn, apparently tracking loud recitation. «وقيل: الطرفان الظهر والعصر. والزلف المغرب والعشاء والصبح كأن هذا القائل راعى جهر القراءة»
#257 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الماوردي · reports · Al-Mawardi reports agreement that the first end of the day is the dawn prayer. «وحكى الماوردي أن الطرف الأول صلاة الصبح باتفاق»
#258 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · rejects · The author says this reported agreement is qualified by the preceding view that does not place dawn at that end. «قلت: وهذا الاتفاق ينقصه القول الذي قبله»
#259 QURTUBI-FULL d.671 · الطبري · prefers · Al-Tabari prefers dawn and sunset as the two ends, arguing that everyone agrees dawn is one end and sunset must be the other. «قال الطبري: والدليل عليه إجماع الجميع على أن أحد الطرفين الصبح»
#260 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · reports · The two ends of the day are morning and evening: dawn prayer is the first prayer near daytime, while the evening prayer may mean afternoon or noon and afternoon; the nearby night prayers are sunset and night prayer. «غدوة وعشية وانتصابه على الظرف لأنه مضاف إليه.»
#261 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · Zulafan are hours near the day, a plural of zulfa; readings include zuluf, zuluf, and zulfa, with the latter meaning one near period. «وساعات منه قريبة من النهار، فإنه من أزلفه إذا قربه وهو جمع زلفة»
#262 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · holds · Good deeds erase sins, and prayer from one prayer to the next expiates what lies between them if major sins are avoided. «يكفرنها. وفي الحديث
" إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر "»
#263 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · رجل · reports · A man told the Prophet that he had done something with a woman but had not had intercourse; this verse was revealed. «أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال إني قد أصبت من امرأة»
#264 BAYDAWI-FULL d.685 · reports · The phrase 'that is a reminder' may refer to steadfastness and what follows or to the Qur'an; it is an admonition for those who take heed. «إشارة إلى قوله { فاستقم } وما بعده وقيل إلى القرآن»
#265 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · The two ends of day mean morning and evening: dawn prayer, and afternoon prayer after noon, which includes noon and afternoon; the night periods near day's end are sunset and night prayers. «﴿ وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار ﴾ غدوة وعشية ﴿ وزلفا من الليل ﴾ وساعات من الليل جمع زلفة»
#266 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · The accusative dual 'ends' functions adverbially because the words are annexed to times, as in phrases giving a whole or half day. «وانتصاب طرفى النهار على الظرف لانهما مضافان إلى الوقت»
#267 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · reports · The five prayers expiate sins committed between them; alternatively good deeds generally erase sins, as in the prophetic instruction to follow an evil deed with a good one. «أن الصلوات الخمس يذهبن الذنوب وفى الحديث أن الصلوات الخمس تكفر»
#268 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · reports · The Prophet also recommends saying 'Glory be to God, praise belongs to God, there is no god but God, and God is greatest.' «أو سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله و الله أكبر»
#269 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · holds · That may refer to the instruction beginning 'remain steadfast' and what follows, or to the Qur'an as admonition for those who take heed. «إشارة إلى فاستقم فما بعده أو القرآن»
#270 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · reports · The verse was revealed about ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyya al-Anṣārī, a date seller who entered a woman's home and kissed her, then repented; the Prophet said his joining the afternoon prayer expiated it, and that the rule applied to everyone. «نزلت فى عمرو بن غزية الأنصارى بائع التمر قال لامرأة فى البيت»
#271 NASAFI-FULL d.710 · النبي · reports · The Prophet asks whether the man prayed the afternoon prayer with them, calls it an expiation, and says this applies to all people, not him alone. «قال عليه السلام هل شهدت معنا العصر قال نعم قال هى كفارة لك»
#272 QASHANI d.736 · holds · The five senses distract the heart with bodily forms and veil it from divine presence; five prayers close those sensory doors, open the heart to God, focus attention, and admit light. «لما كانت الحواس الخمس شواغل تشغل القلب بما يرد عليه من الهيئات الجسمانية»
#273 QASHANI d.736 · holds · Prayer's incoming light removes the darkness and residue of sensory distractions, meaning that good deeds remove evil deeds. «وهذا معنى قوله: { إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات } وقد ورد»
#274 QASHANI d.736 · عليه السلام · reports · A prophetic report says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided. «إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر»
#275 QASHANI d.736 · holds · Praying at both ends of the day lets gathered presence and light persist through other times and remove their fragmentation, sustaining continual prayer. «لينسحب حكمها ببقاء الجمعية واستيلاء الهيئة النورية في أوله إلى سائر الأوقات»
#276 QASHANI d.736 · holds · Natural powers dominate at night, drawing the soul to bodily management and sleep and away from spiritual perception; wakefulness and prayer refine and illuminate them. «لما كانت القوى الطبيعية المدبرة لأمر الغذاء سلطانها في الليل»
#277 QASHANI d.736 · holds · These prayer times and removal of sins remind those who remember their state of clarity, gathered attention, intimacy, and spiritual taste. «تذكير لمن يذكر حاله عند الحضور مع الله في الصفاء والجمعية»
#278 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · The statement إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات was revealed concerning Nabḥān al-Tammār. «وقوله: إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات نزلت في نبهان التمار»
#279 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الليث · reports · Al-Layth defines زلفة as a portion of the first part of night and gives زلف as its plural. «الزلفة قال الليث: طائفة من أول الليل، والجمع الزلف»
#280 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ثعلب · reports · Thaʿlab says زلف are the first hours of night and زلفة is singular. «وقال ثعلب: الزلف أول ساعات الليل، واحدها زلفة»
#281 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · أبو عبيدة، والأخفش، وابن قتيبة · reports · They gloss زلف as the hours and periods of night, each hour being a زلفة; al-Ajjaj's verse illustrates the word's repeated plural form. «وقال أبو عبيدة، والأخفش، وابن قتيبة، الزلف ساعات الليل وآناؤه، وكل ساعة زلفة»
#282 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · زلفة derives from nearness and approach, as shown by the related forms meaning to bring near and draw close. «وأصل الكلمة من الزلفى وهي القربة»

item.aggregated_output:
<<notes for 11_114, part 7 of 0..12>>
#283 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says the verse was revealed after a man had relations with a non-maḥram woman short of intercourse. «سبب نزولها ما في صحيح مسلم من حديث الرجل الذي عالج امرأة أجنبية»
#284 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · A further view takes Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as the boundaries and dawn, Maghrib, and ʿIshāʾ as night prayers, apparently grouping them by recitation aloud or quietly. «وقيل: هما الظهر والعصر، والزلف المغرب والعشاء والصبح، وكأن هذا القائل راعى»
#285 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Another account says the verse predated the incident and the Prophet applied it to that man; when asked whether it was only for him, he said it was for everyone. «وقيل: نزلت قبل ذلك، واستعملها الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في قصة هذا الرجل»
#286 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Addressing the Prophet directly in commands to do good, while directing prohibitions to the community, is a mark of eloquence. «حيث كان بأفعال الخير توجه الخطاب إليه، وحيث كان النهي عن المحظورات» [filed under 11:112, 11:114]
#287 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · The commanded prayer is the obligatory prayer; إقامة means maintaining it continuously, performing it fully, or performing it at its best times. «ولا خلاف أن المأمور بإقامتها هي الصلوات المكتوبة، وإقامتها دوامها، وقيل: أداؤها على تمامها، وقيل: فعلها في أفضل أوقاتها»
#288 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · طرفي النهار is an adverbial accusative; because each طرف belongs to the thing it bounds, the apparent referents are dawn and afternoon. «فالذي يظهر أنهما الصبح والعصر، لأنهما طرفا النهار»
#289 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The fasting rule that dawn belongs to daytime supports dawn as one boundary: deliberate eating or intercourse after dawn invalidates the fast and entails makeup and expiation. «على أن من أكل أو جامع بعد طلوع الفجر متعمدا أن يومه يوم فطر»
#290 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الحسن وقتادة والضحاك · reports · They identify the two daytime prayers as dawn and ʿAṣr, and the night approaches as Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, leaving Ẓuhr outside this verse. «وممن قال: هما الصبح والعصر الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، وقال: الزلف المغرب والعشاء»
#291 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب · reports · They assign the first boundary to dawn and the second to Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, with Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at night; the passage says dawn is not included in this verse. «وقال مجاهد ومحمد بن كعب: الطرف الأول الصبح، والثاني الظهر والعصر»
#292 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن عباس والحسن · reports · They identify the boundaries as dawn and Maghrib and the night prayer as ʿIshāʾ, excluding Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr. «وقال ابن عباس والحسن أيضا: هما الصبح والمغرب، والزلف العشاء»
#293 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الطبري · prefers · Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās’s dawn-and-Maghrib interpretation; Abū Ḥayyān objects that Maghrib belongs to night, so calling it a daytime boundary requires metaphor. «ورجح الطبري قول ابن عباس: وهو أن الطرفين هما الصبح والمغرب، ولا نجعل المغرب»
#294 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Hasanāt can mean all good deeds, especially obligatory prayers and Ramadan fasting; sayyiʾāt in this reading means minor sins, as supported by the sound report about avoiding major sins. «والظاهر عموم الحسنات من الصلوات المفروضة، وصيام رمضان، وما أشبههما من فرائض الإسلام. وخصوص السيئات وهي الصغائر»
#295 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين · reports · Most early interpreters identify the good deeds specifically as the five prayers; Mālik adopts this interpretation, and ʿUthmān illustrates it while performing ablution. «وذهب جمهور المتأولين من الصحابة والتابعين: إلى أن الحسنات يراد بها الصلوات الخمس»
#296 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · مجاهد · reports · Mujāhid interprets the good deeds as the formulas of remembrance: glorifying and praising God, proclaiming his oneness and greatness, and declaring reliance on him. «وقال مجاهد: الحسنات قول الرجل: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله»
#297 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · These interpretations should be understood as examples; the five prayers are the greatest deeds. «وينبغي أن يحمل هذا كله على جهة المثال في الحساب، ومن أجل أن الصلوات الخمس هي أعظم الأعمال»
#298 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Minor sins are erased only when one repents and does not persist in them, a position stated explicitly by the most discerning legal theorists. «والصغائر التي تذهب هي بشرط التوبة منها وعدم الإصرار عليها، وهذا نص حذاق الأصوليين»
#299 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · Erasing sins means expiating minor sins, not making past acts cease to have happened. «ومعنى إذهابها: تكفير الصغائر، والصغائر قد وجدت وأذهبت الحسنات ما كان يترتب عليها»
#300 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Another explanation is that good deeds graciously help people leave sins rather than erase sins already committed, as prayer restrains indecency and wrongdoing. «وقيل: المعنى إن فعل الحسنات يكون لطفا في ترك السيئات، لا أنها واقعة كقوله: إن الصلاة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر»
#301 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · prefers · The demonstrative ذلك most apparently points to the nearest command: establishing prayer at these times as a reminder for those who take heed. «والظاهر أن الإشارة قوله ذلك، إلى أقرب مذكور وهو قوله: أقم الصلاة أي إقامتها»
#302 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · reports · Other referents for ذلك are the news that good deeds erase sins, earlier commands and prohibitions, or the Qurʾān; al-Zamakhsharī gives the earlier counsel as his view and al-Ṭabarī points to this sūrah's commands. «وقيل: إشارة إلى الإخبار بأن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات، فيكون في هذه الذكرى حضا على فعل الحسنات»
#303 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī takes dawn as the morning prayer, Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr as afternoon prayers, and Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ as the night approaches. «وقال الزمخشري: غدوة وعشية قال: وصلاة الغدوة الصبح، وصلاة العشية الظهر والعصر»
#304 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · rejects · Calling the period after noon ʿashiyy does not make Ẓuhr a boundary, since the command names the day's two boundaries rather than morning and afternoon. «ولا يلزم من إطلاق العشي على ما بعد الزوال أن يكون الظهر طرفا»
#305 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الجمهور · reports · The majority read zulafan with an open lām. «وقرأ الجمهور: وزلفا بفتح اللام، وطلحة وعيسى البصرة»
#306 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · طلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر · reports · These readers use a damma on the lām, as though the word were a singular noun. «وطلحة وعيسى البصرة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر: بضمها كأنه اسم مفرد»
#307 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · ابن محيصن ومجاهد · reports · They read the lām quiescent; a further transmission from them has zulfa on the fuʿlā pattern, a feminine singular meaning a station or degree. «وقرأ ابن محيصن ومجاهد: بإسكانها، وروي عنهما: وزلفى على وزن فعلى»
#308 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The plural readings treat the word as successive stations or as a collective noun; zulafā is equivalent to one zalfa. «فزلف جمع كظلم، وزلف كبسر في بسر، وزلف كبسر في بسرة، فهما اسما جنس»
#309 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · holds · The apparent syntax coordinates the night approaches with the two daytime boundaries as another bounded period. «والظاهر عطف وزلفا من الليل على طرفي النهار، عطف طرفا على طرف»
#310 ABUHAYYAN-FULL d.745 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī explains zulaf as the part of the day near nightfall; another interpretation makes it night prayers of devotion and coordinates it with الصلاة instead. «وقال الزمخشري: وقد ذكر هذه القراآت وهو ما يقرب من آخر النهار من الليل»
#311 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · ثعلب · reports · Thaʿlab defines زلفة as the first hours of the night. «والزلفة: أول ساعات الليل، قاله ثعلب.»
#312 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الأخفش وابن قتيبة · reports · Al-Akhfash and Ibn Qutayba use زلف for the night hours generally, with every hour counting as a zulfa. «وقال الأخفش وابن قتيبة: " الزلف:»
#313 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · العجاج · reports · Al-Ajjaj's verse uses زلفا زلفا for successive portions of night. «وقال العجاج:
2729 ناج طواه الأين مما وجفا طي الليالي زلفا فزلفا»
#314 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · The root conveys nearness: أزلفه فازدلف means to bring near and draw close, also used in الشعراء 26:64 and the cited hadith. «وأصل الكلمة من " الزلفى " وهو القرب، يقال: أزلفه فازدلف، أي: قربه فاقترب.»
#315 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الراغب · reports · Al-Raghib says zulfa can mean rank or favor, can euphemistically denote punishment like بشارة, and gives the related meanings of steps and the name Muzdalifa. «وفي الحديث: " ازدلفوا إلى الله بركعتين "»
#316 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · من الليل is an adjective modifying زلفا. «وقال الراغب: " والزلفة: المنزلة والحظوة، وقد استعملت الزلفة في معنى العذاب»
#317 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · طرفي النهار is an adverb governed by أقم; attaching it to الصلاة as the times when prayer occurs is weaker. «طرفي النهار }: ظرف ل " أقم ". ويضعف أن يكون ظرفا للصلاة»
#318 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · holds · طرف is not inherently a temporal adverb, but acquires that case after إضافة to a time expression, as in أول النهار and نصف الليل. «وقرأ العامة " زلفا " بضم الزاي وفتح اللام، وهي جمع " زلفة "»
#319 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · العامة · reports · The common reading زلفا has zay with damma and lam with fatha, a plural of زلفة with a still lam. «وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن أبي إسحاق بضمها، وفي هذه القراءة ثلاثة أوجه»
#320 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · أبو جعفر وابن أبي إسحاق · reports · Their doubled-vowel reading can be a plural of زلفة with vowel harmony, a singular on the pattern of عنق, or a plural of زليف. «وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن بإسكان اللام. وفيها وجهان»
#321 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · مجاهد وابن محيصن · reports · They read زلفا with a still lam, either as a shortened vocalized form or as an original collective noun. «وقرأ مجاهد وابن محيصن أيضا في رواية " وزلفى " بزنة " حبلى "»
#322 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · مجاهد وابن محيصن · reports · They also read زلفى as a singular feminine adjective for a near rank or hour; al-Zamakhshari equates it with زلفة. «وقال الزمخشري: " والزلفى بمعنى الزلفة، كما أن القربى بمعنى القربة "»
<<part 7 ends; continues in part 8>>

item.aggregated_output:
<<notes for 11_114, part 8 of 0..12>>
#323 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · prefers · زلفا most clearly coordinates with طرفي as a time adverb for the near hours of night; another parse coordinates it with الصلاة as an object. «وفي انتصاب " زلفا " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه نسق على " طرفي "»
#324 SAMIN-DURR d.756 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhshari allows coordination with الصلاة, meaning night prayers that draw worshippers near to God. «قال الزمخشري: بعد أن ذكر القراءات المتقدمة " وهو ما يقرب من آخر النهار ومن الليل»
#325 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn ʿAbbas, Hasan, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identify the two ends of day as morning and sunset prayers. «قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: يعني الصبح والمغرب»
#326 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · الحسن · reports · Hasan in another report, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others identify the prayers as dawn and afternoon. «هي الصبح والعصر»
#327 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and al-Dahhak in another report identify them as dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers. «وقال مجاهد: هي الصبح في أول النهار، والظهر والعصر من آخره»
#328 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Hasan, and others take the night approaches to mean the night prayer. «يعني صلاة العشاء»
#329 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · الحسن · reports · Hasan in another report, along with Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatada, and al-Dahhak, identifies them as sunset and night prayers; a prophetic report calls these the night's two approaches. «هما زلفتا (1) الليل: المغرب والعشاء»
#330 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · The verse may predate the five daily prayers prescribed on the Night Journey: initially two daily prayers and night vigil were required, then night vigil was abrogated for the community, remained for the Prophet, and, in one view, was later abrogated for him too. «وقد يحتمل أن تكون هذه الآية نزلت قبل فرض الصلوات الخمس ليلة الإسراء»
#331 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · holds · Good deeds erase earlier sins, as shown by reports that a sinner who performs ablution and prays two units is forgiven. «إن فعل الخيرات يكفر الذنوب السالفة»
#332 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · علي بن أبي طالب · reports · The Prophet says a Muslim who sins, performs ablution, and prays two rakʿas is forgiven; Abu Bakr affirmed that he heard this from the Prophet. «سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ما من مسلم يذنب ذنبا، فيتوضأ ويصلي ركعتين، إلا غفر له»
#333 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · عثمان بن عفان · reports · In the two Sahih collections, Uthman demonstrates the Prophet's ablution and says that performing it and praying two units without distracting thoughts forgives prior sins. «وقال: "من توضأ نحو وضوئي هذا، ثم صلى ركعتين لا يحدث فيهما نفسه، غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه»
#334 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · عثمان بن عفان · reports · Another report from Uthman says each prayer forgives sins committed since the previous prayer, and ablution and dawn prayer forgive the night; these are good deeds that erase sins. «وهن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات»
#335 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو هريرة · reports · The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river at one's door: just as dirt would not remain, the prayers erase sins. «وكذلك الصلوات الخمس، يمحو الله بهن الذنوب والخطايا»
#336 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو هريرة · reports · The five prayers, one Friday to the next, and one Ramadan to the next expiate sins between them when major sins are avoided. «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: "الصلوات الخمس، والجمعة إلى الجمعة، ورمضان إلى رمضان، مكفرات ما بينهن إذا (3) اجتنبت الكبائر"»
#337 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو أيوب الأنصاري · reports · The Prophet says each prayer removes the sins that preceded it. «إن كل صلاة تحط ما بين يديها من خطيئة»
#338 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو مالك الأشعري · reports · The Prophet says prayers were made expiations for what lies between them, citing the verse that good deeds remove evil deeds. «عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "جعلت الصلوات كفارات لما بينهن؛ فإن الله قال»
#339 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · In one account a man confesses kissing a woman; the Prophet recites the verse and says its promise applies to all his community. «عن ابن مسعود؛ أن رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة»
#340 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · In another account the man describes kissing and embracing a woman without intercourse; after the Prophet recalls him and recites the verse, ʿUmar or Muʿadh asks whether it is only for him, and the Prophet says it is for everyone. «جاء رجل إلى النبي (1) صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله»
#341 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet says God distributes character as He distributes provision: He grants worldly life to those He loves and those He does not, but grants faith only to those He loves; faith requires a surrendered heart and tongue and a neighbor safe from harm. «قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله قسم بينكم أخلاقكم (3) كما قسم بينكم أرزاقكم»
#342 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The same report says illicit wealth is not blessed or accepted as charity and becomes provision for Hell; God erases evil with good, since evil cannot erase evil. «إن الله لا يمحو السيئ بالسيئ، ولكنه يمحو السيئ بالحسن»
#343 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · إبراهيم · reports · Ibrahim reports an unnamed Ansari who had sexual contact with a woman short of intercourse; the Prophet could not answer until this verse was revealed, then recited it to him. «عن إبراهيم قال: كان فلان ابن معتب رجلا من الأنصار، فقال»
#344 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · ابن عباس · reports · Reports differ over the man's identity: Ibn ʿAbbas names ʿAmr ibn Ghaziya al-Ansari al-Tammar; Muqatil says Abu Nufayl ʿAmir ibn Qays; al-Khatib says Abu al-Yusr Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr. «وعن ابن عباس: أنه عمرو بن غزية الأنصاري التمار»
#345 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · ابن عباس · reports · A man who had done less than intercourse with a woman brought his case first to ʿUmar and Abu Bakr, then the Prophet; after the verse came, ʿUmar said its remedy was for everyone, and the Prophet affirmed him. «بل للناس عامة. فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "صدق عمر"»
#346 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو اليسر كعب بن عمرو الأنصاري · reports · A woman came to buy dates; Abu al-Yusr invited her inside and kissed her, then confessed to ʿUmar, Abu Bakr, and the Prophet, who reproached him for betraying a man away fighting; Gabriel brought the verse, which applies to all. «أتتني امرأة تبتاع مني بدرهم تمرا»
#347 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · معاذ بن جبل · reports · A man who touched an unlawful woman in every way short of intercourse was told by the Prophet to make a careful ablution and pray; the verse came, and the Prophet said it applied to all Muslims. «فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "توضأ وضوءا حسنا، ثم قم فصل"»
#348 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · يحيى بن جعدة · reports · A mursal report tells of a Companion who found a woman at a pool, touched her short of intercourse, regretted it, and confessed; the Prophet told him to seek forgiveness and pray four units, then recited the verse. «فأخبره بما صنع، فقال له: "استغفر ربك، وصل أربع ركعات"»
#349 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو أمامة · reports · A man asking to receive God's prescribed penalty was ignored until after prayer; the Prophet asked whether he had performed ablution and prayed with them, then said he was cleansed like a newborn and must not repeat the sin. «فإنك من خطيئتك كما ولدتك أمك، ولا تعد»
#350 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · سلمان الفارسي · reports · The Prophet shook a dry branch so its leaves fell and likened this to a Muslim whose careful ablution and five prayers shed sins; he recited the verse. «عن أبي عثمان قال: كنت مع سلمان الفارسي تحت شجرة، فأخذ منها غصنا يابسا»
#351 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · معاذ بن جبل · reports · The Prophet tells Muʿadh to follow a bad deed with a good one that erases it, and to treat people with good character. «عن معاذ، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: "يا معاذ، أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها»
#352 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو ذر · reports · The Prophet gives Abu Dharr the same counsel: fear God everywhere, follow a bad deed with a good one, and treat people well. «وقال الإمام أحمد، رضي الله عنه: حدثنا وكيع، حدثنا سفيان، عن حبيب، عن ميمون بن أبي شبيب، عن أبي ذر»
#353 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أبو ذر · reports · The Prophet advises Abu Dharr to follow every sin with a good deed to erase it and says that proclaiming there is no god but God is the best of good deeds. «هي أفضل الحسنات»
#354 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أنس بن مالك · reports · A report says whoever says there is no god but God at any hour has the sins in the record erased until good deeds balance them; Ibn Kathir notes that Uthman al-Waqqasi is weak. «عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ما قال عبد: لا إله إلا الله، في ساعة من ليل»
#355 IBNKATHIR-FULL d.774 · أنس · reports · A man says he has left no need or small matter undone; the Prophet asks whether he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His Messenger, and says this testimony covers it all; this route is unique through Mastur. «قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأني رسول الله؟»
#356 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Zulaf are groups, stages, or periods of night; they may mean the early obligatory night vigil, or Maghrib and Isha with witr or night vigil. «يمكن أن يكون المراد به التهجد , فقد كان مفروضا في أول الإسلام»
#357 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · All acts of obedience grounded in faith, including prayer, erase minor sins; major sins require repentance, while merely avoiding them expiates only with a sound intention. «الطاعات كلها الصلاة وغيرها المبنية على أساس الإيمان»
#358 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · Prayer is the highest expiation for the weakness and lassitude that cause minor sins, and after faith it is the best act of worship and the broadest aid to uprightness. «وذلك يدل على أنها بعد الإيمان أفضل العبادات»
<<part 8 ends; continues in part 9>>

item.aggregated_output:
<<notes for 11_114, part 9 of 0..12>>
#359 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The two ends of the day mean morning and afternoon prayers, as prescribed in Mecca before the Night Journey; noon may also be intended as the second end. «بالصبح والعصر كما كان مفروضا بمكة في أول الأمر قبل الإسراء»
#360 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Ibn Masud reports that after a man confessed to kissing a woman, the Prophet recited this verse and said it applies to whoever among his community acts by it. «عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أم رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة»
#361 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas regards the verse as belonging to the Meccan and Medinan portions of the surah; the cited report supports that view. «وهذا الحديث يؤيد قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن هذه الآية من هذه السورة المكية المدنية»
#362 BIQAI-FULL d.885 · holds · The preceding exhortation, warning, consolation, and instruction in the remedy for misery form a great reminder for those able to attend, reflect clearly, and understand deeply. «الأمر العالي الرتبة الذي تقدم من الترغيب والترهيب والتسلية وتعليم الداء والدواء»
#363 DURR-FULL d.911 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid identifies the day prayers as dawn, noon, and afternoon, and the night intervals as sunset and night prayers. «عن مجاهد في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: صلاة الفجر وصلاتي العشاء يعني الظهر والعصر»
#364 DURR-FULL d.911 · مجاهد · reports · Mujahid also glosses the night intervals as successive hours, referring to the late night prayer. «عن مجاهد في قوله {وزلفا من الليل} قال: ساعة بعد ساعة يعني صلاة العشاء الآخرة»
#365 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas preferred delaying the night prayer and would cite “and at intervals of the night.” «عن ابن عباس أنه كان يستحب تأخير العشاء ويقرأ {وزلفا من الليل}»
#366 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas identifies the two ends of the day as sunset and dawn prayers, and the night intervals as the late evening prayer. «عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: صلاة المغرب والغداة {وزلفا من الليل}»
#367 DURR-FULL d.911 · الحسن · reports · Hasan identifies the ends of the day as dawn and afternoon prayers, and the night intervals as sunset and night prayers; he says the Prophet called the latter the two night intervals. «عن الحسن في قوله {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} قال: الفجر والعصر {وزلفا من الليل} قال: هما زلفتان»
#368 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet applies the prayer instruction to everyone, not only the man in the preceding account. «فقرأ عليه {وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} الآية فقال معاذ بن جبل: يا رسول الله أله وحده أم للناس كافة»
#369 DURR-FULL d.911 · أبو اليسر · reports · Abu al-Yusr says he kissed a woman who came to buy dates, confessed to Abu Bakr and Umar, then told the Prophet, who reproached him; the verse was revealed and applied generally. «عن أبي اليسر قال أتتني امرأة تبتاع تمرا فقلت: إن في البيت تمرا أطيب منه»
#370 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · A man who asked for punishment was told after praying with the Prophet that he was cleansed of his sin like a newborn; the verse was revealed then. «عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله أقم في حد الله»
#371 DURR-FULL d.911 · معاذ بن جبل · reports · Mu'adh reports a man asking about intimate contact with a woman short of intercourse; the verse was revealed in response. «عن معاذ بن جبل قال: رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ما ترى في رجل لقي امرأة لا يعرفها»
#372 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · In Mu'adh's account, the Prophet prescribed careful ablution and prayer and said the instruction applies generally to believers. «فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توضأ وضوءا حسنا ثم قم فصل قال معاذ: فقلت يا رسول الله»
#373 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · A man confessed to touching a woman whose husband was away on campaign; Umar insisted the revealed prayer instruction applied to all believers, and the Prophet agreed. «عن ابن عباس قال جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن امرأة جاءت تبايعني»
#374 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · Another report says a man confessed to having done something with a woman short of intercourse, after which the prayer verse was revealed. «عن ابن عباس قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إني نلت من امرأة»
#375 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · A man who desired a woman tried to approach her while she bathed in a pool, but his organ became limp; the Prophet prescribed four prayer cycles, and the verse was revealed. «عن ابن عباس أن رجلا كان يحب امرأة فاستأذن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حاجة»
#376 DURR-FULL d.911 · بريدة · reports · A date seller led an Anṣari woman home and pressured her, then regretted sexual contact short of intercourse; the Prophet prayed with him, explained the five prayers named in the verse, and said its cleansing applies to everyone. «عن بريدة قال جاءت امرأة من الأنصار إلى رجل يبيع التمر بالمدينة وكانت امرأة حسناء جميلة»
#377 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet says the prayers expiate sins committed between them, citing the verse. «عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جعلت الصلوات كفارات لما بينهن»
#378 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet says each prayer removes the sins that came before it. «عن أبي أيوب الأنصاري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل صلاة تحط ما بين يديها من خطيئة»
#379 DURR-FULL d.911 · عثمان · reports · Uthman reports that successive prayers after ablution erase sins from the interval since the previous prayer; he identifies the verse's good deeds as these acts and the enduring good deeds as declarations of remembrance. «عن عثمان قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوضأ ثم قال من توضأ وضوئي هذا»
#380 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river: they wash away sins as bathing removes dirt. «عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أرأيتم لو أن بباب أحدكم نهرا»
#381 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet says God does not erase an evil deed by another evil deed, but erases it by a good deed. «عن ابن مسعود قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن الله لا يمحو السيء بالسيء ولكن السيء بالحسن»
#382 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas says a fresh good deed is especially effective in pursuing and overtaking an old sin. «عن ابن عباس قال: لم أر شيئا أحسن طلبا ولا أحسن إدراكا من حسنة حديثة لسيئة قديمة»
#383 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet tells Mu'adh to follow a bad deed with a good deed so it will erase it. «عن معاذ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: يا معاذ أتبع السيئة الحسنة تمحها»
#384 DURR-FULL d.911 · عطاء بن أبي رباح · reports · A man kissed a woman who came to buy flour and regretted it; the verse was revealed, and Ata says it refers to the obligatory prayers. «عن عطاء بن أبي رباح قال: أقبلت امرأة حتى جاءت إنسانا يبيع الدقيق لتبتاع منه»
#385 DURR-FULL d.911 · إبراهيم النخعي · reports · Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says Ibn Muqib confessed to touching a woman short of intercourse; the Prophet waited for guidance, then recited the verse to him. «عن إبراهيم النخعي قال جاء فلان بن مقيب رجل من الأنصار فقال: يا رسول الله دخلت على امرأة»
#386 DURR-FULL d.911 · سليمان التيمي · reports · A man who struck a woman's backside asked Abu Bakr, Umar, and the Prophet about expiation; none knew until the verse was revealed. «عن سليمان التيمي قال: ضرب رجل على كفل امرأة ثم أتى إلى أبي بكر وعمر فسألهما عن كفارة ذلك»
#387 DURR-FULL d.911 · يزيد بن رومان · reports · A man from Banu Tamim kissed and touched a woman, then consulted the caliphs and Prophet; the verse was revealed, and his continued remembrance explains “a reminder for those who remember.” «عن يزيد بن رومان أن رجلا من بني تميم دخلت عليه امرأة فقبلها ووضع يده على دبرها»
#388 DURR-FULL d.911 · يحيى بن جعدة · reports · A man attempted sex with a woman beside a pool but became impotent; the Prophet told him to seek forgiveness, pray four cycles, and recited the verse. «عن يحيى بن جعدة أن رجلا أقبل يريد أن يبشر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمطر فوجد امرأة جالسة على غدير»
#389 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet compares sins falling through the five prayers after good ablution to dry leaves shaken from a branch. «عن سلمان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ غصنا يابسا من شجرة فهزه حتى تحات ورقه»
#390 DURR-FULL d.911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم · reports · The Prophet describes the daily prayers washing away sins at each prayer time and says nothing is recorded during sleep until waking. «عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تحترقون فإذا صليتم الصبح غسلتها»
#391 DURR-FULL d.911 · أبو عبيدة بن الجراح · reports · Abu Ubayda urges matching old sins with new good deeds; even sins as vast as heaven and earth can be overcome by a good deed. «عن أبي عبيدة بن الجراح أنه قال: بادروا السيئات القديمات بالحسنات الحديثات»
#392 DURR-FULL d.911 · الحسن · reports · Hasan likewise urges using new good deeds against old sins, citing the verse as proof. «عن الحسن قال: استعينوا على السيئات القديمات بالحسنات الحديثات»
#393 DURR-FULL d.911 · الحسن · reports · The mindful are those who remember God in prosperity and adversity, hardship and ease, health and illness. «عن الحسن في قوله {ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين} قال: هم الذين يذكرون الله في السراء والضراء»
#394 DURR-FULL d.911 · ابن جريج · reports · Ibn Jurayj says the man who kissed the woman remembered the deed afterward, illustrating the verse's “reminder for those who remember.” «عن ابن جريج قال: لما نزع الذي قبل المرأة تذكر فذلك قوله {ذلك ذكرى للذاكرين}»
#395 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Sins are impurities and acts of obedience purify; ablution washes away sins with its drops, so some jurists considered used ablution cloth impure and disliked praying in it. «أن الذنوب كلها نجاسات والطاعات مطهرات وبماء أعضاء الوضوء تتساقط الأوزار»

<<notes for 11_114, part 10 of 0..12>>
#396 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · A report has God tell Moses that each drop of ablution water used by Aḥmad and his community earns a garden as broad as the sky. «يتوضأ أحمد وأمته كما أمرتهم وأعطيهم بكل قطرة»
#397 BURSEVI d.1127 · الحافظ · reports · Ḥāfiẓ's Persian couplet praises prayer and devoted appeal purified by tears and heart's blood. «خوشا نماز ونياز كسى كه ازسردرد بآب ديده»
#398 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The highest good deed is knowledge of God, following monotheism, and opposing the lower self; remembrance purifies souls and hearts, strengthens obedience, and defeats Satan's schemes. «العلم بالله ، وطريقه التوحيد ، وخلاف هوى النفس»
#399 BURSEVI d.1127 · النبي · reports · When companions ask whether ‘There is no god but God’ is a good deed, the Prophet says it is the best of good deeds. «لا إله إلا الله من الحسنات قال»
#400 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The verse signals constant remembrance, worship, and obedience by day and night, with time for human needs, daytime work, and sleep to restore tired faculties for worship. «وفي الآية إشارة إلى إدامة الذكر والطاعة والعبادة في الليل والنهار»
#401 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · In the inward reading, light from good deeds, remembrance, and watchfulness at day edges and night approaches erases the darkness of time spent on bodily needs. «أي أن أنوار الحسنات وهي الأعمال الصالحة والذكر والمراقبة»
#402 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The luminous spirit would be lost through attachment to the dark body unless sacred good works nurture it, lift it toward spirituality and divine unity, and dispel bodily darkness. «تعلق الروح النوراني العلوي بالجسد الظلماني السفلي موجب لخسران الروح»
#403 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · He compares this nurture to a seed that would be lost unless water made one seed into seven hundred, with God multiplying further as He wills. «كما أن إلقاء الحبة في الأرض موجب لخسران الحبة»
#404 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · One reading assigns the afternoon edge of day to noon and afternoon prayers, and the night approaches to sunset and night prayers, covering all five daily prayers. «الظهر والعصر لأن ما بعد الزوال عشى»
#405 BURSEVI d.1127 · النبي · reports · The Prophet compares five daily prayers to bathing five times in a river at one's door, which leaves no dirt behind. «لو أن نهرا بباب أحدكم يغتسل منه كل يوم خمس مرات»
#406 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · Another reading takes the day's ends as morning and sunset and night approaches as night prayer plus tahajjud, obligatory for the Prophet; it cites the night vigil command. «وفسر بعضهم طرفي النهار بالصبح والمغرب وزلف الليل بالعشاء»
#407 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · Other interpretations include witr according to Abū Ḥanīfa, or night prayer, witr, and tahajjud together, matching the plural ‘approaches.’ «أو الوتر على ما ذهب إليه أبو حنيفة أو مجموع العشاء والوتر والتهجد»
#408 BURSEVI d.1127 · reports · A similar passage is read as morning before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, and sunset and night prayers at night. «أي : بصلاة الصبح [ق : 39-79]»
#409 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Good deeds, especially the five prayers, erase consequences of minor sins rather than undoing sins already committed; prayers, Fridays, and Ramadans expiate between them when major sins are avoided. «على الإطلاق لا سيما الصلوات الخمس»
#410 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · Prayer also restrains people from committing sins, as another verse says it keeps one from indecency and wrongdoing. «إن الصلوة تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر»
#411 BURSEVI d.1127 · أبو اليسر الأنصاري · reports · Abū al-Yusr was tempted by a woman buying dates; he drew her home, embraced and kissed her but stopped before intercourse when she warned him to fear God, then regretted it. «أن أبا اليسر الأنصاري كان يبيع التمر فأتته امرأة»
#412 BURSEVI d.1127 · أبو بكر · reports · Abū al-Yusr confessed to Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, who advised concealing the sin and repenting, but he could not keep silent and went to the Prophet. «فأتى أبا بكر رضي الله عنه فأخبره»
#413 BURSEVI d.1127 · holds · The Prophet told him to wait for God's command; after the afternoon prayer the verse came, and prayer expiated his act for everyone. «فلما صلى صلاة العصر نزلت هذه الآية»
#414 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Ṭalḥa, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and Abū Jaʿfar read zuluf with a rounded lām; Mujāhid and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with a silent lām, and a variant has zulfa, a synonymous form. «وقرأ طلحة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو جعفر ( زلفا ) بضم اللام»
#415 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Good deeds expiate sins and remove liability, not sins as entities; another view says their records are erased. The view that they prevent sinning is remote and contrary to reports. «أي يكفرنها ويذهبن المؤاخذة عليها وإلا فنفس السيئات أعراض وجدت فانعدمت»
#416 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · The apparent scope is obligatory and voluntary good deeds, though some restrict it to obligations. Reports about affirmation matching angels, fasting ʿArafa, and gratitude after eating or dressing support voluntary acts as expiators. «والظاهر أن المراد من الحسنات ما يعم الصلوات المفروضة وغيرها من الطاعات»
#417 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · أبو اليسر · reports · The occasion is reported as Abū al-Yusr regretting he kissed a woman; after waiting for revelation, the Prophet said prayer atoned for it. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn al-Musayyib also transmit this view. «أبا اليسر من الأنصار قبل امرأة ثم ندم فأتى»
#418 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · prefers · Those who identify good deeds as obligatory prayers likely cite one important instance in the general category; the occasion does not restrict the verse. «والظاهر أن ذلك منهم إقتصار على بعض مهم من أفراد ذلك العام وسبب النزول لا يأبى العموم»
#419 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Establish the prescribed prayers fully; other reported meanings are to maintain them regularly or perform them at the start of their times. «أي المكتوبة ومعنى إقامتها أداؤها على تمامها»
#420 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · The two ends mean the beginning and end of the day. Zulf are hours near the day; al-Layth and Thaʿlab say the first part of night, while Abū ʿUbayda, al-Akhfash, and Ibn Qutayba say any night hour, supported by al-ʿAjjāj’s verse. «فإنه من أزلفه إذا قربه»
#421 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Zulf is coordinated with the two ends, and min al-layl qualifies it. End prayers are variously dawn and afternoon, dawn and sunset, or dawn then noon and afternoon; Abū Ḥayyān favors dawn and afternoon, while noon as an endpoint is questioned. «وهو عطف على ( طرفي النهار ) و ( من الليل ) في موضع الصفة له»
#422 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Most identify the night prayers as sunset and evening; a report via al-Ḥasan from Ibn ʿAbbās specifies ʿatama. Another reading makes zulf night prayers drawing near to God, perhaps the Prophet’s night prayer or evening and witr. «والمراد بصلاة الزلف عند الأكثر صلاة المغرب والعشاء»
#423 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · reports · Most take ‘sins’ as minor sins and say major sins require repentance, citing Muslim’s report through al-ʿAlāʾ that five prayers expiate the interval if major sins are avoided. «والمراد بالسيآت عند الأكثرين الصغائر لأن الكبائر لا يكفرها»
#424 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · البلقيني · reports · Al-Balqīnī says 4:31 concerns avoiding major sins throughout life, whereas the prayer report concerns each day; al-Samhūdī objects that lifelong avoidance entails daily prayer, then discusses multiple expiators retaining their rewards. «وأجاب البلقيني بأن ذلك غير وارد لأن المراد بالآية أن تجتنبوا في جميع العمر»
#425 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · rejects · Al-Ālūsī rejects a lifelong reading of 4:31: the reward for avoiding major sins at each time expiates minor sins committed then, as al-Qāḍī and al-Ghazālī support. «والظاهر أن المراد من ذلك أن ثواب إجتناب الكبائر في كل وقت يكفر الصغائر»
#426 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الغزالي · reports · Al-Ghazālī says restraint expiates only when someone has ability and desire to commit a major sin; abstaining from incapacity or lack of desire does not earn that effect. «إجتناب الكبيرة إنما يكفر الصغيرة إذا إجتنبها مع القدرة والإرادة»
#427 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · النووي · reports · Al-Nawawī says that when an expiatory act coincides with major sins but no minor sins, one may hope that the major sins are lightened. «أنه صادف فعل المكفر كبيرة أو كبائر ولم يصادف صغيرة»
#428 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · prefers · Al-Ālūsī reconciles the evidence by making avoidance of major sins a limit on expiating all interval sins, not a condition for any expiation: prayers expiate minors and all interval sins when majors are avoided. «ما اجتنبت الكبائر في الخبر ليس قيدا لأصل التكفير بل لشمول التكفير سائر الذنوب التي بين الصلوات الخمس»
#429 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · ابن حجر · reports · Ibn Ḥajar says avoiding major sins entails performing the five prayers, since abandoning prayer is major; al-Ālūsī says this argument merits examination. «وعلى تقدير ورد السؤال فالتخلص عنه سهل وذلك لأنه لا يتم إجتناب الكبائر إلا بفعل الصلوات الخمس»
#430 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · المحب الطبري · reports · Al-Muḥibb al-Ṭabarī records two views: the majority make avoidance of major sins a condition; another treats it as an exception, so expiation excludes major sins, which he calls stronger. «إختلف العلماء في أمر تكفير الصغائر بالعبادات هل هو مشروط بإجتناب الكبائر على قولين»
#431 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الزركشي · reports · Al-Zarkashī reports disagreement over requiring repentance for expiation; al-Baḥr says the requirement is explicit among rigorous legal theorists. «ذكر الزركشي أنهم إختلفوا في أن التكفير هل يشترط فيه التوبة أم لا»
#432 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · السبكي · reports · Al-Subkī says acceptance of repentance from unbelief is certain by grace, but acceptance for sins is disputed; other authorities differ over whether its expiation is presumptive or certain. «والمنقول عن السبكي أنه قال : إن قبول التوبة عن الكفر مقطوع به تفضلا»

<<notes for 11_114, part 11 of 0..12>>
#433 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · أهل السنة · reports · Al-Nasafī, Ṣadr al-Sharīʿa, and other Sunni scholars allow punishment for minor sins even when major sins are avoided, citing 4:48 and 18:49; the Muʿtazila deny it based on 4:31, which may concern unbelief. «أن العقاب على الصغائر جائز الوقوع سواء إجتنب مرتكبها الكبائر أم لا»
#434 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · صاحب الذخائر · reports · The author of al-Dhakhāʾir argues that some good deeds expiate minor and major sins, citing reports promising forgiveness of past and future sins; Ibn al-Mundhir leans this way. «وذهب صاحب الذخائر إلى أن من الحسنات ما يكفر الصغائر والكبائر»
#435 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · rejects · Critics call broad expiation ignorance and agreement with the Murjiʾa, arguing repentance would be pointless; al-Ālūsī replies that expiation differs from Murjiʾism and repentance remains obligatory for new and recurring delay sins. «إن الكبائر والصغائر تكفرها الطهارة والصلاة لظاهر الأحاديث»
#436 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Past expiation does not remove the ongoing duty to repent, just as a sleeper whose prayer time passed must still make it up; the Abū Hurayra report is specific and cannot be extended by analogy. «ولا يلزم من تكفير الله تعالى ذنوب عبده سقوط التكليف بالتوبة التي كلف بها تكليفا مستمرا»
#437 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الأشعري · reports · Repentance for minor sins is obligatory according to al-Ashʿarī, with al-Juwaynī and al-Anṣārī reporting consensus; ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām says delay incurs renewed sin over time. «التوبة من الصغائر واجبة على ما نقل عن الأشعري وحكى إمام الحرمين وتلميذه الأنصاري الإجماع عليه»
#438 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · The reminder benefits those who heed admonition, singled out because they are the ones who benefit. «أي عظة للمتعظين وخصهم بالذكر لأنهم المنتفعون بها»
#439 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الزمخشري · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī says ‘that’ refers to the counsel about uprightness, avoiding tyranny and inclination toward wrongdoers, and establishing prayer at the named times; Abū Ḥayyān prefers prayer alone. «والإشارة إلى ما تقدم من الوصية بالإستقامة والنهي عن الطغيان والركون إلى الذين ظلموا»
#440 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الطبري · reports · Al-Ṭabarī takes the reference as the sūrah’s commands and prohibitions; others identify the Qurʾān, or prayer and repentance. «إشارة إلى الأوامر والنواهي في هذه السورة»
#441 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · الواسطي · reports · Al-Wasiti says the lights of acts of obedience remove the darkness of acts of disobedience. «قال الواسطي : أنوار الطاعات تذهب بظلم المعاصي»
#442 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · يحيى بن معاذ · reports · Yahya ibn Muʿadh says God covers a believer's sin, then forgives it, then replaces it with good deeds, citing 25:70. «وقال يحيى بن معاذ : إن الله سبحانه لم يرض للمؤمن بالذنب حتى ستر ولم يرض بالستر حتى غفر»
#443 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · Prayer at the stated times and good deeds erasing wrongs remind those who remember God of presence, purity, gatheredness, intimacy, and spiritual taste. «ذكرى للذاكرين تذكير لمن يذكر حاله عند الحضور مع الله تعالى في الصفاء والجمعية والأنس والذوق»
#444 ALUSI-FULL d.1270 · holds · The command is to establish the prescribed prayer at its known times; prayer is the believer's ascent, as reports attest its lofty rank. «أمر بإقامة الصلاة المفروضة على ما علمت وقد ذكروا أن الصلاة معراج المؤمن وفي الأخبار ما يدل على علو شأنها»
#445 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · “Zulaf” is the plural of “zulfa,” whose Arabic broken plural denotes at least three; with two parts of the day, this indicates five prayers, including three during the night’s approaches to day. «“Zülef” “zülfe”nin cem‘i ve Arabîde cem‘in ekalli üç olduğu için bununla ikisi gündüz tarafında, üçü de geceden olmak üzere tam beş vakit namaz emredilmiş olduğu zâhirdir»
#446 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · Each prayer is a good deed that continually erases prior minor sins; the five daily prayers expiate sins between them when major sins are avoided, as a hadith states. «beş vakit namaz arada vâki‘olan küçük günahlara keffaret olur»
#447 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · A hadith says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided. «namaz, namaza kadar aralarındakine keffarettir, kebâirden ictinab ettikçe»
#448 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · Because prayer restrains indecency and evil, regular prayer cultivates aversion to sins, avoidance of major sins, and remorse and repentance for any major sin already committed. «namaza devam edildikçe ale’l-umûm seyyiâta karşı hiss-i nefret uyanır»
#449 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · “That” may refer to the prayer or to the address from the command to be steadfast through this passage; either way, it is a reminder for people who heed. «O namaz yahut فَٱسْتَقِمْ emrinden buraya kadar olan hitâbe»
#450 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · The positive commands are addressed grammatically to the Prophet but apply to everyone, while prohibitions address the community; this rhetorical shift implies that transgression and inclination to oppressors are inconceivable for the Prophet but possible among his community. «zâhiren müfred olarak Resûlullah’a hitab edilmiş, hâlbuki mâna itibariyle emir, umûma yapılmıştır» [filed under 11:112, 11:113, 11:114]
#451 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · On the reading that dawn counts among night prayers, the two day parts are noon and afternoon, while the three night-adjacent times are sunset, evening, and dawn; the author links this arrangement to 17:78. «“tarafeyi’n-nehâr”dan murad öğle ve ikindi, “zülefen mine’lleyl” de akşam, yatsı, sabah»
#452 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · Noon and afternoon can be called the day’s two parts because dawn is its root, sunrise to noon its body, and noon through afternoon its prominent later divisions; another verse also speaks of the day’s parts. «Sabah gündüzün kökü, Güneş’in tulû‘undan zevâline kadar da gövdesi, zevalden sonra öğle ve ikindi de gurûbuna kadar tehavvülâtının bariz hadleri»
#453 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · Most scholars instead take the phrase as dawn and afternoon, or morning and sunset, supported by the wording “before sunrise and before sunset”; this leaves noon, which other verses state explicitly, unmentioned here. «sabah ve ikindi olması lâzım geleceğine kāil olmuşlardır»
#454 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · Al-Zamakhsharī and many others read one day part as before noon and the other as after it, yielding dawn, noon, and afternoon within the two parts and incorporating dawn as one of the day’s parts. «Sâhib-i Keşşâf gibi birçokları da bir tarafı zevalden evveli, bir tarafı da zevalden sonrası yani gudüv ve aşiy mânasına hamletmişlerdir»
#455 ELMALILI d.1361 · reports · On that interpretation, the three night parts imply six obligatory prayers: the Prophet’s additional obligatory tahajjud and the community’s witr; other plural wording also suggests at least six. «farz namazların beş değil altı olması iktizâ eder»
#456 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · Five prayers are certain through several proofs, while a sixth is only probable; therefore witr is a practical obligation (wājib), not an obligation of belief. «farz-ı i‘tikādî değil farz-ı amelî»
#457 ELMALILI d.1361 · prefers · Elmalılı prefers taking the two day parts as two of the customary three divisions, noon and afternoon, because the opposing “night approaches” clarify the phrase; with sunset, evening, and dawn, this gives the five daily prayers. «gündüzün iki ucu veya ortasının iki yanı demek olmayıp örfte başlıca üç sayılan etrâf-ı nehârdan ikisi demek olması bizce»
#458 ELMALILI d.1361 · holds · These five prayers are established and performed with congregation; the call announcing the prayer is sunnah and congregational prayer is wājib. «tam beş vakit namazdır ki ikāmet ve cemaatle kılınır. İkāmet sünnet, cemaat vâcibdir»
#459 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · The statement that good deeds remove sins explains the command to establish prayer; in context, “indeed” emphasizes the claim and signals its causal force. «مسوقة مساق التعليل للأمر بإقامة الصلوات»
#460 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · Removing sins can mean good habits make sin easier to avoid, as prayer restrains indecency, or that good deeds erase guilt after a sin; both apply broadly. «وإذهاب السيئات يشمل إذهاب وقوعها بأن يصير انسياق النفس إلى ترك السيئات سهلا»
#461 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · prefers · Here “sins” means minor sins, limited by verses that exempt minor lapses and promise their erasure when major sins are avoided. «ومحمل السيئات هنا على السيئات الصغائر التي هي من اللمم»
#462 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Bukhari reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who illicitly kissed a woman and asked the Prophet about it; the verse was revealed, and the Prophet said it applies to anyone in his community who does such a deed. «عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أن رجلا أصاب»
#463 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · عبد الله بن مسعود · reports · Tirmidhi reports Ibn Masud's account of a man who confessed intimate contact short of intercourse; the Prophet later recited the verse and said it applies to everyone, not only that man. «عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : جاء رجل»
#464 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · الترمذي · reports · Al-Tirmidhi grades the Ibn Masud report hasan sahih; he also gives two reports, from Muadh and Abu al-Yusr, and calls those weak. «قال الترمذي : هذا حديث حسن صحيح»
#465 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · ابن عباس · reports · Ibn Abbas and Qatada used the report's “it was revealed to him” wording to argue that this verse, unlike the rest of the surah, is Medinan. «حمل ابن عباس وقتادة على القول بأن هذه الآية مدنية دون بقية هذه السورة»
#466 IBNASHUR-FULL d.1393 · holds · If that wording is literal, the verse was inserted here because it fits the preceding command to be upright and the following command to be patient. «هذه الآية ألحقت بهذه السورة في هذا المكان»

#469 TABATABAI d.1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام · reports · A report identifies the two ends of the day as sunset and dawn prayers and the night periods as the late evening prayer. «وفيه عن جرير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال»
#470 TABATABAI d.1402 · أبو جعفر عليه السلام · reports · A report from Zurara connects the verse to the five daily prayers; al-Tabataba'i says it suggests the day's two sides mean periods before and after noon. «وفي التهذيب بإسناده عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث في الصلوات الخمس اليومية»
#471 TABATABAI d.1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام · reports · A report explains that a believer's night prayer removes sins committed during the day; the author notes parallel transmissions in several collections. «قال صلاة المؤمن بالليل تذهب بما عمل من ذنب النهار»
#472 TABATABAI d.1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم · reports · In a report narrated by Salman, the Prophet shakes a dry branch and says that good ablution followed by the five prayers sheds a Muslim's sins like falling leaves. «هكذا فعله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأنا معه تحت شجرة»
#473 TABATABAI d.1402 · علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام · reports · Ali recounts a man confessing a sin; after the man prayed with the Prophet following good ablution, the Prophet told him the prayer expiated the sin. «عن الحارث عن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم»
#474 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · The confession story circulates through many Companion routes with variations; al-Tirmidhi reports it from Abu al-Yusr, who experienced it. «والرواية مروية بطرق كثيرة عن ابن مسعود وأبى أمامة ومعاذ بن جبل وابن عباس»
#475 TABATABAI d.1402 · أحدهما عليهما السلام · reports · When Ali asks which verse gives Muslims most hope, he dismisses several proposed forgiveness verses and identifies the command to establish prayer. «عن أبى حمزة الثمالى قال سمعت أحدهما عليهما السلام يقول إن عليا عليه السلام أقبل على الناس»
#476 TABATABAI d.1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم · reports · The report says five prayers wash away sins like a river cleans dirt, leaving the worshiper cleansed as at birth after each prayer. «إنما منزلة الصلوات الخمس لأمتي كنهر جار على باب أحدكم»
#477 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · The prayer-as-river simile is also transmitted in Sunni collections from Companions including Abu Hurayra, Anas, Jabir, and Abu Sa'id. «وقد روي المثل المذكور في آخر الحديث من طرق أهل السنة عن عدة من الصحابة كأبي هريرة وأنس وجابر»
#478 TABATABAI d.1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام · reports · Abu Abdillah warns that angels record each deed; small sins should not be dismissed, and a good deed can erase an old grave sin, as the verse teaches. «عن إبراهيم الكرخي قال كنت عند أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فدخل عليه رجل من أهل المدينة»
#479 TABATABAI d.1402 · أبو عبد الله عليه السلام · reports · Asked whether charity and pilgrimage from officials' earnings erase the sin, Abu Abdillah says one sin does not cancel another, but a good deed cancels sin. «عن سماعة بن مهران قال سأل أبا عبد الله عليه السلام رجل من أهل الجبال»
#480 TABATABAI d.1402 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم · reports · A report says a Muslim who performs ablution and obligatory prayer well is forgiven for sins committed since the preceding prayer. «عن أبى أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم»
#481 TABATABAI d.1402 · holds · Good deeds, especially prescribed prayers, remove traces of sins from believers' souls; this teaching serves as a reminder for those who remember God. «تعليل لقوله وأقم الصلاة وبيان أن الصلوات حسنات واردة على نفوس المؤمنين»
#482 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The literal phrase is at the two ends of the day. «at the two ends»
#483 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · The command covers the obligatory prayers whose forms and exact times are set by the Prophet's authenticated sayings and practice: dawn, after midday, afternoon, sunset, and early night. «both of which are clearly laid down in the sunnah»
#484 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · holds · Because the verse stresses prayer's importance generally, Asad takes it to include remembrance of God throughout waking life, beyond the five obligatory prayers. «it is safe to assume that it refers not merely to the five obligatory prayers but to a remembrance of God at all times»
#485 ASAD-NOTES d.1412 · Rashid Rida' · rejects · Rashid Rida' rejects the proposed Medina dating of verses 12, 17, and 114 as unconvincing and holds the whole surah Meccan. «this view as unconvincing and holds that the surah in its entirety was revealed at Mecca» [filed under 11:12, 11:17, 11:114]
#486 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The closing section states why the stories were told and guides the Prophet and companions; Quraysh must learn from local history or face the same consequences. «The Quraysh are warned to learn a lesson from the history of their country» [filed under 11:101-123]
#487 ISLAHI-TADABBUR · holds · The sūrah as a whole is a comprehensive sermon directed toward one prescribed purpose. «the whole of it is a comprehensive sermon on a prescribed purpose» [filed under 11:1-123]
#488 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Day runs from dawn to sunset and night from sunset to dawn; the day’s two edges are dawn and sunset. #489 KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · holds · Zulef, plural of zulfa, means the night’s early hours near day and refers here to the night prayer; because the verse gives no form or exact times, it stresses prayer at the indicated periods without detailing them, as Shawkani notes. «“Gündüze yakın saatler” diye tercüme ettiğimiz zülef kelimesi ise zülfenin çoğulu olup gecenin gündüze yakın olan ilk saatlerini ifade eder»

#494 STUDYQURAN · the Prophet · reports · The Prophet teaches that a good deed following an evil deed erases it. «Follow up an evil deed with a good deed»
#495 STUDYQURAN · the Prophet · reports · The heart is polished by remembrance of God; prayer and remembrance can affect a heart darkened by sin. «In a ḥadīth the Prophet said, “For everything there is a polish, and the polish of the heart is the remembrance of God”»
#496 STUDYQURAN · reports · One identification of the two day-end prayers is dawn and sunset. «the prayers at the two ends of the day are interpreted to be the prayers performed at dawn»

#499 STUDYQURAN · reports · The early-night prayers may collectively mean sunset and night prayers. «the early hours of the night can collectively refer to the prayers performed at sunset and during the night»
#500 STUDYQURAN · reports · Alternatively, the early-night phrase may refer only to the night prayer. «or to the latter only (IK)»
#501 STUDYQURAN · holds · The range of interpretations of the five prayers resembles the disagreement over which prayer is the middlemost at 2:238. «A similar range of opinion regarding the five prayers can be seen in identifying the middlemost prayer in 2:238»
#502 STUDYQURAN · the Prophet · reports · The daily prayers expiate minor sins committed between them, provided major sins are avoided. «the Prophet is reported to have said, “Verily from prayer to prayer there is an expiation»
#503 STUDYQURAN · holds · More generally, the positive effects of good deeds can counterbalance the negative effects of evil deeds. «In a more general sense, it can refer to the manner in which the positive effects of good actions can offset the negative effects of evil actions»
#504 STUDYQURAN · holds · The sūrah encourages the Prophet and believers to persist in the prescribed prayers. «to persist in the prescribed prayers (v. 114)»
